title: "Clustered heatmaps in JavaScript with CanvasXpress"
description: "Build an interactive, clustered gene-expression heatmap with dendrograms and sample annotations from a matrix — a few lines of browser JavaScript, one portable spec."

---

The clustered heatmap is the default way to look at an expression matrix: rows and columns reordered
by similarity, dendrograms on the margins, and sample metadata alongside. CanvasXpress clusters
inside the render, so in the browser you pass a plain matrix and get an interactive, reproducible
figure.

## Load the library

```html
<link href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/neuhausi/canvasXpress@69.6.1/inst/htmlwidgets/lib/canvasXpress/canvasXpress.css" rel="stylesheet">
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/neuhausi/canvasXpress@69.6.1/inst/htmlwidgets/lib/canvasXpress/canvasXpress.min.js"></script>
```

## The markup and the spec

Genes are the variables (rows), samples the columns; the matrix goes in as `data`, and the sample
annotation becomes a track over the columns. `samplesClustered` / `variablesClustered` turn on
hierarchical clustering with dendrograms.

```html
<canvas id="heatmap" width="650" height="550"></canvas>
<script>
  // standard normal via Box–Muller
  function gauss() {
    var u = 0, v = 0;
    while (u === 0) u = Math.random();
    while (v === 0) v = Math.random();
    return Math.sqrt(-2 * Math.log(u)) * Math.cos(2 * Math.PI * v);
  }

  var ng = 40, ns = 30, genes = [], samps = [], cond = [], matrix = [];
  for (var j = 0; j < ns; j++) { samps.push("S" + (j + 1)); cond.push(j < ns / 2 ? "Tumor" : "Normal"); }
  for (var i = 0; i < ng; i++) {
    genes.push("Gene" + (i + 1));
    var row = [];
    for (var k = 0; k < ns; k++) {
      var val = gauss();
      if (i < 20 && cond[k] === "Tumor")   val += 2;        // first block up in Tumor
      if (i >= 20 && cond[k] === "Normal") val += 2;        // second block up in Normal
      row.push(Math.round(val * 1000) / 1000);
    }
    matrix.push(row);
  }

  var data = {
    y: { vars: genes, smps: samps, data: matrix },
    x: { Condition: cond }
  };

  var config = {
    graphType: "Heatmap",
    samplesClustered: true, variablesClustered: true,
    colorSpectrum: ["navy", "white", "firebrick3"],
    showSmpDendrogram: true, showVarDendrogram: true,
    title: "Clustered expression heatmap"
  };

  new CanvasXpress("heatmap", data, config);
</script>
```

## Live result

```{=html}
<link href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/neuhausi/canvasXpress@69.6.1/inst/htmlwidgets/lib/canvasXpress/canvasXpress.css" rel="stylesheet">
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/neuhausi/canvasXpress@69.6.1/inst/htmlwidgets/lib/canvasXpress/canvasXpress.min.js"></script>
<canvas id="heatmapLive" width="650" height="550"></canvas>
<script>
(function () {
  function gauss() {
    var u = 0, v = 0;
    while (u === 0) u = Math.random();
    while (v === 0) v = Math.random();
    return Math.sqrt(-2 * Math.log(u)) * Math.cos(2 * Math.PI * v);
  }
  function draw() {
    if (typeof CanvasXpress === "undefined") { return setTimeout(draw, 60); }
    var ng = 40, ns = 30, genes = [], samps = [], cond = [], matrix = [];
    for (var j = 0; j < ns; j++) { samps.push("S" + (j + 1)); cond.push(j < ns / 2 ? "Tumor" : "Normal"); }
    for (var i = 0; i < ng; i++) {
      genes.push("Gene" + (i + 1));
      var row = [];
      for (var k = 0; k < ns; k++) {
        var val = gauss();
        if (i < 20 && cond[k] === "Tumor")   val += 2;
        if (i >= 20 && cond[k] === "Normal") val += 2;
        row.push(Math.round(val * 1000) / 1000);
      }
      matrix.push(row);
    }
    new CanvasXpress("heatmapLive",
      { y: { vars: genes, smps: samps, data: matrix }, x: { Condition: cond } },
      { graphType: "Heatmap", samplesClustered: true, variablesClustered: true,
        colorSpectrum: ["navy", "white", "firebrick3"],
        showSmpDendrogram: true, showVarDendrogram: true,
        title: "Clustered expression heatmap" });
  }
  draw();
})();
</script>
```

Rows and columns are reordered by similarity, the dendrograms show the clustering, and the samples
separate cleanly by condition. Hover a cell for its gene, sample and value; the whole figure is one
portable spec you can store, validate and re-render from R or Python.
